column1: 1:1|An oracle concerning Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum of Elkosh.|Preserves both oracle and written vision designations without locating uncertain Elkosh.

1:2|The LORD is a jealous and avenging God;
the LORD avenges and is full of wrath.
The LORD takes vengeance on his adversaries
and reserves wrath for his enemies.|Retains three divine names and repeated vengeance rather than softening the opening.

1:3|The LORD is slow to anger and great in power,
but he will certainly not leave guilt unpunished.
The LORD’s way is in whirlwind and storm;
clouds are the dust of his feet.|Keeps patience alongside accountability and ancient storm/feet imagery.

1:5|Mountains quake before him,
and hills melt away.
The earth heaves before him—
the world and everyone living in it.|Keeps geological disturbance and universal inhabitants rather than reducing to local tremor.

1:6|Who can stand before his indignation?
Who can endure his burning anger?
His fury pours out like fire;
rocks break apart before him.|Preserves paired questions and liquid fire/rock imagery.
1:7|The LORD is good,\na stronghold on the day of distress.\nHe knows those who take refuge in him.|Keeps relational knows and stronghold rather than flattening into general reassurance.
1:8|But with an overwhelming flood\nhe will make a complete end of her place;\ndarkness will pursue his enemies.|Retains feminine unnamed her place and darkness as the pursuing subject.

1:9|What are you plotting against the LORD?\nHe is making a complete end;\ndistress will not rise a second time.|Preserves complete end refrain and ambiguous second-time distress rather than a universal promise of no suffering.
1:10|Though entangled like thorns\nand drunk with their drink,\nthey will be consumed like fully dried stubble.|Keeps the difficult thorn/drunkenness comparison and complete dryness.
1:11|From you came one who plotted evil against the LORD,\na counselor of wickedness.|Leaves the male plotter unnamed and belial descriptive rather than a supernatural proper name.

1:12|This is what the LORD says:
“Though they are at full strength and so numerous,
they will be cut down and pass away.
Though I have afflicted you,
I will afflict you no more.|Keeps enemies' strength and the shift to afflicted feminine addressee, explained in notes.
1:13|Now I will break his yoke from your neck\nand tear your bonds apart.”|Preserves male oppressor versus female captive pronouns and physical liberation images.

1:14|The LORD has commanded concerning you:
“No more descendants will carry your name.
From the house of your gods
I will cut off carved and cast images.
I will prepare your grave, for you are worthless.”|Marks switch to masculine enemy address and retains lineage, cult objects, and grave judgment.

1:15|Look, on the mountains,
the feet of one bringing good news, announcing peace!
Celebrate your festivals, Judah; fulfill your vows.
The wicked one will never again pass through you;
he is utterly cut off.|Preserves messenger's feet and explicit Judah addressee, mapping source2:1 correctly.
2:1|A scatterer has come up against you.\nGuard the fortress! Watch the road!\nBrace your waist! Gather all your strength!|Keeps four urgent defensive commands and scatterer as unnamed attacker.

2:2|For the LORD is restoring Jacob’s splendor,
like Israel’s splendor,
though plunderers have plundered them
and ruined their vine branches.|Preserves like rather than silently and, and repeated plunder plus vine image.

2:3|His warriors’ shields are red;
his soldiers are clothed in scarlet.
The chariots flash with fiery metal on the day he prepares them,
and cypress spears are brandished.|Renders two rare equipment terms cautiously with uncertainty noted; retains color and preparation.

2:4|Chariots race wildly through the streets
and rush about the squares.
They look like torches;
they dart like lightning.|Keeps both locations and two rapid light similes.

2:5|He summons his nobles;
they stumble as they go.
They hurry to her wall,
and the protective screen is set in place.|Keeps unnamed commander, stumbling, and uncertain siege screen without fixing attacker/defender identification.
2:6|The river gates are opened;\nthe palace dissolves.|Retains terse water and dissolution imagery without inventing the engineering of Nineveh's fall.

2:7|It is decreed: she is exposed and led away.\nHer slave women moan like doves,\nbeating their breasts.|Chooses passive decree rather than proper name Huzzab; preserves female captives and mourning gesture.

2:8|Nineveh has been like a pool of water since her earliest days,
but now they are fleeing.
“Stop! Stop!”
No one turns back.|Follows difficult since-her-days wording and repeated futile command.
2:9|Plunder silver! Plunder gold!\nThere is no end to the treasure,\na wealth of every precious object.|Retains doubled plunder imperative and abundant loot.

2:10|Empty, emptied, devastated!
Hearts melt, knees buckle;
every waist writhes,
and every face loses its color.|Uses sound-linked English for three Hebrew devastation words and preserves all bodily reactions.

2:11|Where is the lions’ den,
the feeding ground of the young lions,
where lion, lioness, and cub walked
with no one to frighten them?|Keeps the whole lion family and ironic lost security without overexplaining royal symbolism in text.

2:12|The lion tore enough prey for his cubs
and strangled prey for his lionesses.
He filled his lairs with prey,
his dens with torn flesh.|Retains repeated prey and violent provision as the empire image.

2:13|“I am against you,” declares the LORD of Armies.
“I will burn her chariots into smoke;
the sword will consume your young lions.
I will cut off your prey from the earth,
and your messengers’ voices will be heard no more.”|Preserves source her/your shift, lion-to-military linkage, and final silencing of messengers.
